learningObjectives: Explain the developmental sequence underlying synaptogenesis.
Identify the principal cells, structures and signals involved in synaptogenesis.
Connect synaptogenesis to later cognition and behaviour.
Interpret clinical findings without treating development as deterministic.

anatomy.label: Growth cone
anatomy.detail: Growth cones sample attractive and repulsive cues as axons navigate.
anatomy.clinical: Guidance errors can disconnect otherwise healthy regions.

anatomy.label: Synaptic adhesion
anatomy.short: Molecules align pre- and postsynaptic partners
anatomy.detail: Cell-adhesion systems stabilise contact and recruit synaptic machinery.
anatomy.clinical: Many risk genes influence synaptic organisation rather than a single transmitter.

anatomy.label: Presynaptic terminal
anatomy.detail: Vesicles, active zones and calcium channels organise at the sending side.
anatomy.clinical: Release probability matures with activity and molecular signalling.

anatomy.label: Postsynaptic density
anatomy.detail: The receiving membrane accumulates receptors and signalling complexes.
anatomy.clinical: Receptor composition changes the strength and meaning of input.

anatomy.label: Pruning and stabilisation
anatomy.detail: Frequently co-active pathways are more likely to stabilise; less useful contacts may weaken or disappear.
anatomy.clinical: Microglia, complement signalling and neural activity all participate in refinement.

interaction.title: Synaptogenesis sequence
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence to follow development over time.

stages.label: Navigate
stages.text: Axons and dendrites reach potential partners.

stages.label: Contact
stages.text: Adhesion systems stabilise an initial junction.

stages.label: Mature
stages.text: Release sites and receptor fields become functional.

stages.label: Refine
stages.text: Activity strengthens, weakens or removes connections.

quizBank.question: Synaptogenesis refers to:
options: Formation and maturation of synaptic contacts
quizBank.explanation: Synaptogenesis builds functional junctions between cells.

quizBank.question: A growth cone primarily:
quizBank.explanation: Growth cones detect cues that steer axons toward or away from targets.

quizBank.question: Synaptic pruning is best understood as:
options: A process limited to old age
quizBank.explanation: Pruning helps optimise developing circuits by removing or weakening selected contacts.

quizBank.question: Activity can influence synaptic development by:
quizBank.explanation: Patterns of activity help determine which synapses mature and persist.

quizBank.question: Which statement is most accurate clinically?
options: Synaptic-development findings are often shared across diagnoses
quizBank.explanation: Synaptic mechanisms are important but rarely specific enough to diagnose a condition alone.
